why: session_id/agent_id/task_summary/outcome/decisions/errors/user_corrections are only interpolated into content strings and metadata dicts passed to store_memory/mistake_note_add, never to a path, command, or query sink.

agent_ids only filters list/dict lookups and builds an os.environ.get() key name (MCP_BOOTSTRAP_FORMATTER_{agent_id}), a safe no-op lookup, not an injection point; get_formatter() dispatches on a fixed env-configured name, not the caller's agent_id.
client_type is used only as a dict key into a hardcoded guides{} map in server_impl.py:141-241, with a safe default fallback; never builds a path or is executed.
limit is only used as a Python list slice ([:limit]) after storage.search_by_tag(['quarantined']); no injection surface.

content_hash reaches storage.update_memory_metadata (storage/mixins/metadata.py:51), which binds it via a parameterized `WHERE content_hash = ?` SQLite query, so no SQL injection; no other sink exists for this argument.

project_path/session_ids give a real arbitrary-file-read primitive (session_ids even allows ../ or absolute-path escape via pathlib, limited to .jsonl-suffixed targets), but MemoryServer.local_only_tools() hides this tool from list_tools and refuses call_tool whenever remote_transport is True, and both run_sse/run_streamable_http set remote_transport=True before serving (verified in utils/startup_orchestrator.py:360,433) plus a redundant check in web/api/mcp.py; only the stdio transport serves it, where the caller already has host filesystem access.

The only caller-controlled argument is batch_size (an int used solely for pagination limits); content sent to the LLM rewriter (harvest/rewriter.py) is the server's own already-stored memory content sent to a fixed, env-configured provider endpoint, which is the tool's advertised distillation purpose, not caller-influenced.

error_pattern/context_signature/incorrect_action/correct_action are only interpolated into a content string passed to store_memory, which persists it via parameterized SQL inserts; no path/command/query interpretation of these fields.
query is only used for semantic retrieval (embedding similarity) via retrieve_memories(); no injection surface.

content_hash reaches storage.get_by_hash/update_memory_metadata (storage/mixins/retrieve.py, metadata.py) via parameterized `WHERE content_hash = ?` queries; the handler also enforces memory_type=='mistake' before any update, matching its own docstring constraint.

content_hash is used only in parameterized SQL lookups/deletes, and the handler verifies memory_type=='mistake' before deleting, so the docstring's 'only deletes mistake notes' claim is actually enforced in services/memory_service.py:1103-1125.

content/metadata/tags are stored as opaque text/JSON via memory_service.store_memory into parameterized SQL; NLI/belief/auto-capture side paths only re-store or re-embed the same content, never execute or resolve it as a path/command.
turns content is concatenated into a plain string and stored via the same parameterized store_memory path as memory_store; session_id/tags are only used as tag strings.

query/tags/time filters flow into storage.search_memories(), whose exact-mode lookup uses a parameterized LIKE ('%' || ? || '%') and semantic/tag paths use bound `?` params throughout (storage/base.py, storage/mixins/retrieve.py); no string concatenation of caller input into SQL.

tags/memory_type/stale_days build a dynamic WHERE clause in storage/mixins/retrieve.py:get_all_memories, but every value (including per-tag LIKE patterns) is passed as a bound `?` parameter with wildcard-escaping (_escape_like), never string-formatted into the SQL.

storage.delete_memories() (storage/base.py:447) requires at least one explicit filter (content_hash/tags/before/after) to prevent accidental mass deletion, supports dry_run preview, and all underlying deletes use parameterized SQL; bulk deletion is the tool's advertised purpose, not an injection or auth-bypass finding.
handle_cleanup_duplicates() takes no caller-controlled arguments at all -- it calls storage.cleanup_duplicates() with no parameters from the `arguments` dict.

content_hash is bound as a `?` parameter in storage.update_memory_metadata/update_memory_versioned (storage/mixins/metadata.py:51); `updates` is merged into a JSON metadata blob or stored as new memory content, never interpreted as code/path/command.

content_hash for 'rate'/'get' actions is only used in storage.get_by_hash/update_memory_metadata (parameterized `?` lookups); 'maintain' orchestrates internal cleanup/conflict/entity-extraction steps using only server-side config, not caller-supplied values reaching a sink.
handle_memory_conflicts ignores its `arguments` dict entirely and just calls storage.get_conflicts() with no caller-controlled input.

winner_hash/loser_hash reach storage.resolve_conflict (storage/mixins/metadata.py:432), which first verifies both hashes exist via a parameterized SELECT before running parameterized UPDATE statements; no string concatenation of the hashes into SQL.
handle_check_database_health never reads from its `arguments` parameter; it only queries internal health/performance state.
handle_get_cache_stats never reads from its `arguments` parameter; it only reports process-global cache counters and static backend config.

hash/hash1/hash2/rel_type/entity_name for every action (connected/path/subgraph/infer/suggest/abduct/list_entities/entity_profile) reach GraphStorage methods in storage/graph.py that bind all values as `?` parameters; the one query built with .format() (find_connected) only inserts fixed JOIN/CASE fragments chosen from a validated 'direction' enum, never caller data, so there is no SQL injection path.
query/tags feed semantic retrieval and graph.find_memories_by_entity/list_entities, all parameterized SQL; entirely read-only per its own docstring.
entity_id/limit/max_hops only drive graph.find_memories_by_entity and graph.common_neighbors lookups (parameterized SQL) and Python-side list slicing; read-only per its own docstring.

time_horizon is checked against a fixed 6-item allow-list before use in every action; the 'merge' action's content_hashes are verified to exist via parameterized get_by_hash before a store-then-delete sequence (also parameterized), so no injection and no data-loss race.

file_path/directory_path are resolved via Path.resolve() but not confined to a base directory -- the real guard is server_impl.py's local_only_tools()/_reject_local_only(), which hides and refuses memory_ingest on any remote transport (fixed for GHSA-7crr-2r7w-cpfm on 2026-09-05); on the local stdio transport (this audit's scope) the caller already has host filesystem access, so no privilege boundary is crossed.
